issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The new RDKit descriptors are computed from the SMILES strings only. The 1st/99th percentile clip bounds come from the training fold only, and the test labels are never touched.
DESC_CACHE is a global cache keyed by SMILES. It holds only label-free descriptor values, so reusing them across folds does not leak information. It just saves compute.
The diff does not show an import of rdkit.Chem.Descriptors. The job finished and scored, so the import must already be in the file. Otherwise it would have crashed.

Small robustness risk: if MolFromSmiles returns None for an invalid SMILES, the descriptor calls will raise an error. That did not happen on this data. Inf and NaN values are handled by nan_to_num and the clipping.
Only the first feature set gets the descriptors (train_sets[0]). That is a design choice, not a bug.

Recomputed z: (0.0906 - 0.0897) / (0.0049 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = 0.0009 / 0.0060 ≈ 0.15. The harness reports 0.162. The gap probably comes from rounding in the shown means (a difference of 0.00085 to 0.00095 gives z of about 0.14 to 0.16) or from a slightly different noise sd. Either way the improvement is well within noise, so the reject decision stands. The change also adds code for a gain that may not be real.
